question.problem:
Determine a set of parametric equations, defined for $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ),$ that generate a vertical parabola that has its vertex at $(0,0)$ and which passes through the point $(-8,8).$ Express your answer in the form $x=2pt,y=p{t}^{2},$ where $p$ is a constant.

$x=$
{{field-1}},
$\,y=$
{{field-2}}
question.worked_solution:
The parametric equations of a vertical parabola  that has its vertex at $(0,0)$ are

$$
x=2pt,\,y=p{t}^{2},
$$

where $p$ is constant.

Since the parabola passes through $(-8,8),$ we can substitute $x=-8$ and $y=8$ into the standard parametric equations to obtain a system of equations. This gives

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-8=2pt \\ 8=p{t}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the first equation for $t,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}-8 & =2pt \\ t & =-\frac{4}{p}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting this into the second equation and solving for $p,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}8 & =p{(-\frac{4}{p})}^{2} \\ 8 & =p\cdot \frac{16}{{p}^{2}} \\ 8 & =\frac{16}{p} \\ p & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the parametric equations of the parabola are

$$
x=2(2)t,\,y=(2){t}^{2},
$$

which simplify to

$$
x=4t,\,y=2{t}^{2}.
$$
